targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands command execution, approval policies and mutable repository configuration.
targetAudience.readerProblem: An action that looks harmless from its command name can execute configured helpers, so a lexical allowlist can silently grant more authority than intended.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change removed Git from known-safe command classification on Unix and Windows after demonstrating that repository configuration can make nominally read-only Git operations execute helpers.

externalHook.description: The visible command expresses intent, but configuration, executable path and policy determine what authority is actually exercised.

coreProposition: For digital employees, a nominal action name is evidence of intent, not execution authority; when configuration, wrappers or environment can redirect behavior, admission must bind executable identity, execution context and governing policy, while approval and effect containment remain separate gates.

originalValue.description: Separates nominal intent, effective execution identity, policy authority and downstream effect containment into distinct auditable facts instead of treating a command label as a complete safety decision.

readerTakeaway: Treat lexical safety as one admission signal, bind authorization to the effective executable and context, version the governing policy, and keep approval separate from sandboxing and effect verification.

supported: The merged Codex implementation removes Git from known-safe classification on Unix and Windows.
Under UnlessTrusted, plain git status reaches approval unless an explicit execution-policy rule authorizes it.
Absolute-path tests distinguish a policy-covered host executable from another unmatched Git path.
An end-to-end test reaches human approval and preserves denial as the command result.
unsupported: That every Git command is unsafe under every policy
That approval proves helper behavior or downstream effect containment
Binary provenance, sandbox integrity or repository-configuration integrity
Independent security validation across agent runtimes
uncertain: The minimum effective-execution evidence required for informed approval
How policy authority should expire when repository state changes

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general execution-governance pattern without relying on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged code and tests establish a concrete failure of lexical safety classification, while the Research Object contributes a reusable and evidence-bounded authority model.
